title: Prime-power coefficient Hom and tensor boundedness criterion
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and $k=\mathbf F_\ell$. Let $K\in D^b(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ have bounded cohomology [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. The following are equivalent: (i) $K$ has finite Tor amplitude [def-kun-tor-amplitude]; (ii) $K\otimes^L_\Lambda k_X$ has bounded cohomology [def-kun-derived-tensor]; (iii) $R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(k_X,K)$ has bounded cohomology [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. When they hold there is a canonical isomorphism
$$R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(k_X,K)\cong K\otimes^L_\Lambda k_X$$
in $D^b(X_{\mathrm{et}},k)$. Neither excellence, invertibility of $\ell$ on $X$, nor constructibility of $K$ is required.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 6.2.2.4, including the two-periodic comparison on pp. 294-295

proof.text: Choose a bounded representative $L$ of $K$, supported in $[a,b]$, by [lem-sfb-bounded-representative]. Use a small skeleton of the small etale site, as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Put $R=\Lambda_X$ and $S=k_X$. Define an augmented complex $P\to S[0]$ by $P^{-j}=R$ for $j\geq0$, zero positive terms, augmentation $R\to S$, and $d^{-j}=\ell$ for odd $j$ and $d^{-j}=\ell^{n-1}$ for positive even $j$. In $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$, $\ker(\ell)=(\ell^{n-1})$ and $\ker(\ell^{n-1})=(\ell)$, so this augmented complex is exact. Exact sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] gives the same conclusion for the constant module sheaves. This includes $n=1$: the two maps are $0$ and $1$. Each term $R$ is flat since $R\otimes_R-$ is the identity, so [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes $P$ K-flat.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 6.2.2.4, bounded representative and alternating resolution underlying the displayed double complex, pp. 294-295

proof.text: Let $A=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R L)$; by [def-kun-derived-tensor] it represents $K\otimes^L_\Lambda k_X$ after forgetting $k$-scalars. The sheaf Hom complex $\mathcal Hom^\bullet_R(P,L)$ represents the underlying $\Lambda$-object of $R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(k_X,K)$. Indeed take $L\to I$ bounded-below injective and K-injective by [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution]. The cone of $L\to I$ is bounded-below acyclic; [lem-sc-bounded-above-finite-free-hom-acyclic] applied to $P$ makes $\mathcal Hom(P,L)\to\mathcal Hom(P,I)$ a quasi-isomorphism. Applying [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] with $t:P\to S$ and the identity of $I$ makes $\mathcal Hom(S,I)\to\mathcal Hom(P,I)$ a quasi-isomorphism. Use [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] for the former complex. Rephase the summand $\mathcal Hom(P^{-p},L^q)=L^q$ by $(-1)^{pq+p(p+1)/2}$. The resulting complex $B$ has horizontal columns $p\geq0$, differential $\ell$ for even $p$ and $\ell^{n-1}$ for odd $p$, and vertical differential $(-1)^p d_L$. The Hom differential gives exactly this rephasing. Thus $A$ vanishes in degrees $>b$, and $B$ vanishes in degrees $<a$.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 6.2.2.4, alternating tensor and Hom half-complexes; Hom comparison uses Stacks 0A95

proof.text: Form the two-sided double complex with a copy of $L$ in each horizontal column $p\in\mathbf Z$, horizontal differential $c^p=\ell^{n-1}$ for even $p$ and $c^p=\ell$ for odd $p$, and total differential $c^p+(-1)^p d_L$. Call its total $C$. In each total degree only $b-a+1$ columns can contribute, so its sums are finite. The two summands of the differential anticommute because consecutive columns have opposite signs, while $\ell^n=0$. Translation $p\mapsto p+2$ gives an actual chain isomorphism $C\cong C[2]$. Projection to columns $p\leq0$ gives $C\twoheadrightarrow A$. Its kernel is the positive-column total, isomorphic to $B[-1]$: in column $p\geq1$ use the scalar $(-1)^{p-1}$ to compare $B[-1]$ with $C$. Hence there is a degreewise split short exact sequence of complexes $0\to B[-1]\to C\to A\to0$. Its connecting map $A\to B$ on column zero is multiplication by $\ell^{n-1}$.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 6.2.2.4, displayed two-sided complex, distinguished triangle and footnote iv; signs and the degreewise split sequence written explicitly

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] to this sequence. Since $B$ vanishes below $a$, $H^q(C)\cong H^q(A)$ for $q<a-1$. Since $A$ vanishes above $b$, $H^q(C)\cong H^{q-1}(B)$ for $q>b+1$. If $A$ is bounded, the first identity makes $H^q(C)=0$ for all sufficiently negative $q$; if $B$ is bounded, the second makes it zero for all sufficiently positive $q$. In either case $H^q(C)\cong H^{q+2}(C)$ forces every cohomology sheaf of $C$ to vanish. Conversely, if $C$ is acyclic, the connecting maps give $H^q(A)\cong H^q(B)$ for every $q$. The upper bound on $A$ and lower bound on $B$ then make both bounded. Thus (ii) and (iii) are equivalent. Forgetting $k$-scalars does not change kernels, images or whether cohomology sheaves vanish, so this is the required boundedness in the $k$-derived categories.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 6.2.2.4, three observations on C and equivalence of its acyclicity with the two boundedness conditions

proof.text: If (i) holds with Tor interval $[u,v]$, substitute the sheaf $k_X$ in [def-kun-tor-amplitude] to get (ii). Conversely assume (ii), with $H^i(K\otimes^L_R S)=0$ outside $[u,v]$ (enlarge the interval if necessary so $u\leq v$). By [lem-kun-flat-resolution-existence] choose a K-flat resolution $Q\to L$ with flat terms. Put $D=Q\otimes_R S$. Then $D$ represents the reduction by [def-kun-derived-tensor], so its cohomology is zero outside $[u,v]$.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 6.2.2.4, the recalled implication (i) iff (ii); expanded using Stacks 06YS and 06YU

proof.text: For an arbitrary $S$-module sheaf $N$, [lem-exc-constant-field-sheaf-tensor-cohomology] gives $H^i(D\otimes_S N)=H^i(D)\otimes_S N$, hence zero outside $[u,v]$. There is an isomorphism of complexes $(Q\otimes_R S)\otimes_S N\to Q\otimes_R N$, sending $(x\otimes s)\otimes y$ to $x\otimes sy$, inverse $x\otimes y\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes y$. These formulas are balanced and commute with differentials. By [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor] tensor sheaves are sheafifications of the sectionwise tensor products; thus these inverse formulas on pure tensors define inverse maps of sheaves. Therefore $H^i(Q\otimes_R N)=0$ outside $[u,v]$.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 6.2.2.4, recalled residue-field test, expanded by the field calculation and nilpotent devissage; Stacks 0GMW

proof.text: For an arbitrary $R$-module sheaf $M$ set $F_sM=\operatorname{im}(\ell^s:M\to M)$, $0\leq s\leq n$. Then $F_0M=M$, $F_nM=0$, and $G_s=F_sM/F_{s+1}M$ is killed by $\ell$. Exact sheafification of the constant quotient sequence identifies $R/\ell R$ with $S$, by [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact]. Hence $G_s$ has a unique $S$-module structure: a local lift of a scalar from $S$ acts through $R$, and two lifts differ by a multiple of $\ell$, which kills $G_s$. Step 6 applies to every $G_s$. This filtration is finite for every module sheaf, without constructibility or finite-generation assumptions.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 6.2.2.4, recalled residue-field Tor criterion: explicit finite filtration by powers of ell

proof.text: For each $s<n$, apply the exact tensor functor with $Q^j$ to $0\to F_{s+1}M\to F_sM\to G_s\to0$ in every degree $j$; exactness is precisely [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], using tensor symmetry. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact], for $i\notin[u,v]$ there is an exact segment $H^i(Q\otimes F_{s+1}M)\to H^i(Q\otimes F_sM)\to H^i(Q\otimes G_s)$. Descending induction on $s$ starts with $F_nM=0$; the right term vanishes by step 6 and the left term by induction, so the middle vanishes. At $s=0$, [def-kun-derived-tensor] identifies this with $H^i(K\otimes_R^L M)=0$. The same interval works for every $M$, giving (i) by [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. This proves all three conditions equivalent.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 6.2.2.4, recalled residue-field Tor test: exact tensoring and finite descending induction; Stacks 0117

proof.text: Suppose the equivalent conditions hold. Apply [lem-sp-ringed-site-tor-flat-model] on the small ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ to choose a bounded complex $F$ of flat $R$-module sheaves representing $K$. No constructibility is required by that statement. By [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site], $F$ is K-flat, so [def-kun-derived-tensor] computes the reduction as $F\otimes_R S=F/\ell F$ in the category of $S$-module sheaves.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 6.2.2.4, last paragraph: bounded flat representative; Stacks 08G1 and 06YQ

proof.text: For a flat $R$-module sheaf $M$, tensor the constant exact sequences $0\to(\ell^{n-1})\to R\xrightarrow{\ell}(\ell)\to0$ and $0\to(\ell)\to R\xrightarrow{\ell^{n-1}}(\ell^{n-1})\to0$ with $M$, also tensoring the inclusions of the two ideals into $R$. Exactness, by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], gives $\ker(\ell:M\to M)=\ell^{n-1}M$ and $\ker(\ell^{n-1}:M\to M)=\ell M$. The ideal sequences are sheafifications of the elementary constant module sequences, by [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact]. Consequently multiplication by $\ell^{n-1}$ gives a natural $S$-linear isomorphism $M/\ell M\to M[\ell]$, where $M[\ell]=\ker(\ell:M\to M)=\mathcal Hom_R(S,M)$, the last identification being evaluation at $1$. These identities hold also for $n=1$, when this is the identity of $M$.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 6.2.2.4, final paragraph, the isomorphism K/ell K to ell-torsion induced by ell^(n-1)

proof.text: Use step 2 with $L=M[0]$ for a flat sheaf $M$. The positive cohomology of the alternating Hom complex is zero by the two kernel-image identities in step 10. Thus $\mathcal Hom_R(S,-)$ has no positive right-derived sheaves on a flat $M$. Regard this left exact additive functor as $G:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(S)$ with the scalar action provided by [lem-weil-pbc-restricted-coefficient-hom], taking its first argument $S$. Both module-sheaf categories have enough injectives by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and $G$ is left exact because maps from $S$ commute with kernels. The same proposition gives their Grothendieck property. Using the bounded-below K-injective resolution of step 2, the underlying $R$-complex of $RG(K)$ is $\mathcal Hom_R(S,I)$, hence is $R\mathcal Hom_R(S,K)$ by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. This also describes its $S$-action. Forgetting that action is exact and detects zero cohomology, so the preceding vanishing proves that every term of $F$ is $G$-right-acyclic. By [lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification], these positive cohomology sheaves are precisely the higher right-derived functors of $G$ on $M$, so this is the acyclicity required in step 12.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 6.2.2.4, final sentence: flat sheaves are acyclic for Hom from k; coefficient action is evaluation on the first argument

proof.text: Apply [src-right-derived-functor-plus-acyclic-unit] to $G$ and the bounded-below complex $F$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $G(F)\to RG(K)$ in $D(S)$. Combining with step 10 termwise yields $K\otimes_R^L S\cong F/\ell F\xrightarrow{\ell^{n-1}}F[\ell]=G(F)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_R(S,K)$ in $D^b(S)$. To specify canonicity without a choice of flat model, on every bounded complex $L$ use the composite of the derived tensor counit, the natural map $L/\ell L\to L[\ell]$ given by $\ell^{n-1}$, and the right-derived unit for $G$. The left derived functor is [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], with its counit and K-flat computation as in [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]; the last unit and its universal property are [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. This composite is natural on the homotopy category and is a map between functors which factor through the derived localization. The universal property of that localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] therefore gives a unique natural morphism on $D^b(R)$. On the flat representative it is exactly the displayed isomorphism. Its inverse is the canonical isomorphism in the orientation of the statement.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 6.2.2.4, final paragraph; naturality made explicit using derived counit/unit and Stacks 05TA
